subject: general
question: Which of the following best reflects the change in sector importance in India over time?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Primary → Secondary → Tertiary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's economy has undergone significant structural changes, transitioning from being predominantly **agriculture-based (Primary Sector)** to an industrial economy (Secondary Sector) and finally to a service-oriented economy (Tertiary Sector).
 
• The **Primary Sector**, which includes agriculture and allied activities, was the most dominant during the early years of independence.
 
• Post-independence, industrialization efforts during the 1950s–70s led to the growth of the **Secondary Sector**, including manufacturing and construction.
 
• In recent decades, the **Tertiary Sector** (services), such as IT, banking, and communication, has become the largest contributor to India's GDP and employment.
 
• This transition reflects India's economic diversification and increasing focus on technology, globalization, and skill-based industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Sector:**

 
 
• Includes agriculture, fishing, forestry, and mining activities.
 
• Relies heavily on natural resources and contributes significantly to rural employment.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Sector:**
 
 
• Includes manufacturing, processing, and construction industries.
 
• India's industrial policies such as the Five-Year Plans emphasized the growth of this sector.
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Sector:**
 
 
• Comprises services such as education, healthcare, IT, banking, transport, and communication.
 
• Contributes the largest share to India's GDP and has been a key driver of economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Economic Shift:**
 
 
• The structural transformation of India's economy is a common pattern observed in developing nations as they progress toward industrialization and service-oriented economies.
 
• This shift impacts employment patterns, urbanization, and overall economic development.
